bull.b: Growth is supported by both customer acquisition and expansion within the installed base. Rising large-customer penetration and 122% net retention indicate that Cloudflare is broadening deployments and increasing account value, supporting recurring revenue durability over the next several quarters.

Improving operating leverage shows that revenue is scaling faster than core expenses, strengthening the path toward sustainable profitability. Lower sales, research, and administrative expense ratios provide room to fund growth while improving earnings conversion as the business expands.

Positive and improving free cash flow gives Cloudflare internally generated funding for network investment, product development, and customer expansion. A substantial cash and securities position also supports resilience while the company transitions from accounting losses toward GAAP profitability.

bear.b: Leverage remains high for a software company and reduces financial flexibility despite the cash balance. Debt obligations can constrain future investment choices and increase sensitivity to slower growth, especially because TTM cash flow covers only a modest portion of the debt load.

Cloudflare has not yet established durable GAAP profitability, even as revenue has grown and non-GAAP results improve. Continued operating losses make the business more dependent on execution and expense discipline, leaving less evidence that earnings power is fully proven.

Lower gross and free-cash-flow margins indicate that rapid growth is currently carrying greater delivery or investment costs. Although gross margin remains within management's target range, sustained compression could limit operating leverage and reduce the cash available to support expansion.
